mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the same month indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.4 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the real savings rate (RSAFS) below 3% for six consecutive months indicates households are drawing down savings to finance consumption, which supports demand and corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.
